subject: Customer outage: sustained 429s + latency — suspected rate-cap sync issue
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@nebulahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production errors — 429s and latency spikes this morning

Ben —

We started seeing elevated 429s and 500ms+ tail latency on our Redwood endpoints around 08:45 PT and it has persisted for ~20 minutes in waves. This is impacting our ingestion pipeline; we're buffering but can't sustain further degradation. Attached a short sample of request traces and a few example responses (nebula_request_samples.log).

Can you confirm this is on your side or if we've misconfigured something? We're running standard production quotas, nothing changed in our deployment.

Sara
Director of Platform, Nebula Health
[attachment: nebula_request_samples.log]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-01T09:25:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production errors — 429s and latency spikes this morning

Looping you in — customer reports sustained 429s and tail latency. They said they didn't change anything. I pulled the sample and see short bursts of immediate 429s after a handful of successful tokens. Looks like requests are being dropped rapidly after a client appears to hit a cap.

Ask: can infra/ratelimit owners check whether the refill/burst windows for the policy tied to Nebula (HP-98234) were updated during the morning deploy? Also want a quick triage on whether gateway-sync vs. central rate engine mismatch could explain this.

Priority: customer is in production (healthcare) and unhappy — please treat as P1 for now. I'll keep Sara updated.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[inline: request samples attached]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-01T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors — 429s and latency spikes this morning

Ben / Karthik —

I pulled the metrics and saw a sudden drop in allowed tokens for Nebula at 08:44:12Z that lines up with their report. The central rate engine shows an on-record policy with a 1-minute refill window and a 500-token burst allowance. However, the regional gateway cache had an older policy with a 15-second refill and zero burst for that customer shard. That would lead to immediate suppression once the short-window tokens were consumed.

I'm attaching a comparison sheet (ratecap_policy_comparison.xlsx) that shows the mismatch. No config change was deployed to Nebula's customer record this morning from the control plane, but we did push a config propagation change to gateways at 08:30 to optimize rule caching. That propagation path might have accidentally pulled a fallback policy for some regional shards.

Immediate mitigation options I've been testing:
- Roll back gateway cache to the previous propagation (30s) — quick, but may re-expose old bug.
- Hotpatch gateway shard to accept central token-bucket parameters (allow burst) — slightly higher risk but more targeted.
- Temporarily raise customer-level soft cap to avoid 429s while we investigate.

Karthik, if you can validate whether hotpatch is safe, I'll coordinate a temporary soft cap increase (30m) and notify the customer.

—Lauren
Senior Prod Ops
[attachment: ratecap_policy_comparison.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-01T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors — 429s and latency spikes this morning

Short summary: likely root cause = gateway caching fallback applied an older token-refill cadence (15s) and dropped burst allowance (0) for ~3 regional shards serving Nebula between 08:38–08:58Z. Central engine was healthy. The mismatch created a scenario where clients could exhaust a tiny local window and get immediate suppression even though central policy permits bursts.

Plan:
1) Approve hotpatch to accept central token parameters on affected gateway shards. This is ~10 minutes to deploy per shard, no schema change.
2) Apply a temporary customer soft cap increase to avoid further 429s while shards rotate (30 minutes).
3) Postmortem: add validation to propagation pipeline to ensure gateway caches cannot fall back to older policy states; add end-to-end check during config pushes.

I'll prepare the hotpatch now. Lauren — please coordinate the soft cap and notify Sara with an ETA. Ben — please prepare a concise customer note (see Marissa's ask below).

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
[inline: I started packaging shard hotpatch]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-01T10:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Production errors — 429s and latency spikes this morning

Sara —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for sending traces. We're seeing the same behavior on our side and the engineering team has identified a policy sync mismatch that caused a small set of gateway shards serving Nebula to fall back to a legacy refill cadence with no burst allowance. We're taking immediate steps:

- Applying a temporary soft cap increase for Nebula to prevent further 429s (30m window while we rotate shards).
- Hotpatching affected gateway shards to accept the central token-bucket parameters (rolling over the next 20 minutes).

I'll keep you posted on progress and will follow up with a short postmortem and remediation plan once we validate stability. Apologies for the disruption — we'll credit back impacted usage for the window.

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[attachment: none]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-03T16:45:00Z
Subject: Postmortem requested & exec note for Nebula Health (HP-98234)

Thanks team — per my review the hotpatch and soft cap worked and Nebula reported error rates back to nominal within ~25 minutes. They accepted the usage credit offer and asked for a short written summary we can include with invoicing.

Please produce a one-page postmortem capturing:
- Root cause in one sentence (policy-propagation fallback caused refills/burst mismatch).
- Timeline with timestamps for detection, mitigation, and full recovery.
- Short list of mitigations we pushed (hotpatch, soft cap, rollback of the propagation change).
- Next steps and owners: propagation validation (Lauren), automated E2E config check (Karthik), customer communication & credit (Ben).

Also include any recommendations for short-term guardrails so sales can communicate risk posture to other enterprise customers in the next T+48 hours. I'll review and sign off before we send to Nebula.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success
[attachment: trace_bucket_snapshot_20290401.tar.gz]
